correctness.rationale: Every rank-at-least-two chain isometry has a unique signed affine extension; summing its restrictions reconstructs the known exact monoid size. Every nonidentity ambient affine isometry fixes at most one point. For two representative supports both at least 3n/4, at least n/2-1 input positions yield a nonfixed transition into the first support. A path-edge greedy matching for translations and a one-edge-per-two-cycle matching for reflections each give at least (n/2-1)/3 independent local witnesses, each ruling out commutation with probability at least 1/8. Conditioning each Bernoulli support on rank >=2 costs at most a factor four. Short types are exponentially rare, giving the claimed uniform exponential bound. The proof also separately counts all 2^n idempotents. Direct finite enumeration n=2..7 checks monoid sizes, pairs, and the idempotent subtraction. No inference from finite cases is used in the infinite proof.

Full text of original 2010 chain paper and 2018 issue / 2023-listed Thai Journal paper were read, and neither states a commuting probability or asymptotic idempotent dominance theorem. published-finding corpus semantic searches identified related restricted interval-domain and rank-of-product results, but no covering statement for the full chain distance-preserving inverse monoid. residual_risks: A general unindexed theorem on commuting probability of inverse semigroups may imply this particular case; no global novelty guarantee.

value.rationale: A genuine nontrivial limit for commuting probability of a natural exponentially large inverse monoid: although non-idempotents form roughly five-sixths of all elements, they contribute an exponentially vanishing fraction of commuting pairs. The positive 1/36 limit and a conditional concentration theorem contrast with known 3/10 behavior for the polynomial-size interval-domain rook monoid. An independent matching obstruction yields a uniform quantitative rate, not a routine count or trivial consequence of size alone.
